title: UploadEnvelope - Wax-Sealed Envelope as Drop Target

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: Mailing a letter: the envelope flap opens to receive contents, and a wax seal pressed shut means it is complete and sealed.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: A WeTransfer-inspired CSS 3D envelope as a file-upload drop target with a four-state machine: idle (closed, 'drop files into the envelope'), drag-over (flap opens via rotateX(180deg) with perspective), uploading (progress fill rises in the envelope body), complete (a wax seal with a checkmark appears and the flap closes). Files visually slide into the pocket.

design_tokens.borders: Envelope pocket cut to a V via clip-path; wax seal as a radial-gradient disc with embossed rim highlight
design_tokens.elevation: True CSS 3D: back panel, letter and pocket layered on separate translateZ planes; flap hinges so it renders in front when closed and behind the letter when open - depth sorting replaces z-index
design_tokens.typography: Invitation-style serif label; functional state copy beside the envelope

interactive_mechanics: Drag-over opens the flap; drag-leave closes it (affordance state, not decoration)
Upload progress rendered as rising fill inside the envelope body
Completion wax-seal stamp with checkmark as the terminal reward state
File drop/slide-in animation into the pocket
usability_notes: The strongest argument in the library for metaphor-as-function: every state of a mundane file upload maps to a physical mail stage, so the drop target's affordance is unmistakable. Implementation notes that transfer: hinge-on-separate-plane solves the flap z-order without z-index; staged transitions belong to the state being entered (flap first, letter delayed 0.45s); keyboard equivalents and tabindex focus must exist for the drop target, and the wax-seal completion must also be announced to AT (role=status). Sibling implementations: James Frewin's drag-to-crack seal envelope and a pure-CSS hinge variant documented down to the transform math.
